answer: New agents start with zero influence and earn it only after several epochs of graded useful work, so a fake cannot wander in and vote on day one. Each identity must produce graded output across six epochs, about 30 hours of compute, before its attestations count. Similarity checks flag clusters whose answers, timing, and funding source match, and no identity may vouch for its own cluster, so a karst of hollow shells collapses when one is caught and the cluster loses its standing. Like an ocean, only proven swimmers pass the break: 1,000 fakes cost 30,000 hours before moving a single vote.
